why: a decorated class is read like any other: bump adds zero to its result (proved, a method of a decorated class); reset writes 1 for 0 (unproved, WITNESS); twice is untouched and unproved: in a decorated class its two calls of bump are transitions (a class decorator may replace the class), keyed by the file's method code, which bump's change changed (lane B: PASS-bounded, bump's result is the same number); clear names the count after its reset, whose text changed (unproved, WITNESS: the call of the decorated reset is a transition whose key carries the file's method code, so a changed method makes it another transition).
